Article Title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister today
Article Text:
Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs will meet PM Modi over breakfast on Friday

KOLKATA/NEW DELHI: Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs, who are now with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and have so far refused to be a part of the BJP-led NDA, will meet PM Narendra Modi over breakfast on Friday.Murshidabad lawmakers Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan met Union minister Amit Shah on Thursday to voice concerns over SIR tribunals and the removal of loudspeakers from mosques.They have so far stayed away from two NDA meetings. The other 17 NCPI legislators, alongside six Shiv Sena MPs who support the NDA, will also meet the prime minister Friday.
Article Summary: Murshidabad lawmakers Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan met Union minister Amit Shah on Thursday. They have so far stayed away from two NDA meetings. The other 17 NCPI legislators, alongside six Shiv Sena MPs who support the NDA, will also meet the prime minister.

Article Title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
Article Text:
Abhishek Banerjee's secretary granted a week long interim bail

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday granted a week-long interim bail to Sumit Roy , personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee , in the Salboni land-grabbing case but asked him to make himself personally available for investigation in the police station concerned without being accompanied by an advocate or other persons.An FIR was registered against Roy after his name cropped up during the interrogation of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra, who was arrested in June. Hazra was accused of selling govt land in Salboni as private land. Roy had allegedly been absconding. The Supreme Court issued notice to the Bengal government on Roy's plea and said, "The petitioner's arrest shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing."
Article Summary: Sumit Roy, personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, granted a week-long interim bail. The Supreme Court issued notice to the Bengal government on Roy's plea and said, "The petitioner's arrest shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing"

Article Title: BJP to Congress: Let House function, Amit Shah will come
Article Text:
Both Rahul and Kharge have repeatedly questioned Shah’s absence from Parliament, demanding a debate on the Ram temple donation theft

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday accused Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge of deliberately spreading a false narrative of home minister Amit Shah not attending Parliament, saying he cannot be a part of its proceedings when the opposition party will not allow the legislature to function through its unceasing protests.Shah is willing to hear the opposition and will reply emphatically, the BJP said. “Shah is present at his office in the Parliament House all day. But you will not allow Parliament to run... He can attend only when you allow it to function,” BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad told reporters in a rejoinder to the LoPs in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha over their constant attack on Shah over the issue.Both Rahul and Kharge have repeatedly questioned Shah’s absence from Parliament, demanding a debate on the Ram temple donation theft and Shah’s statement on Delhi police’s excesses against student protesters.
Article Summary: The BJP accused Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge of deliberately spreading a false narrative of home minister Amit Shah not attending Parliament. Both Rahul and Kharge have repeatedly questioned Shah’s absence from Parliament, demanding a debate on the Ram temple donation theft. Shah is willing to hear the opposition and will reply emphatically, the BJP said.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET protest crackdown, says students were forced to apologise
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET crackdown

NEW DELHI: Standing with a group of youngsters who faced police action during the NEET protests , Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Wednesday said the ruling party is sending goons to the homes of students and forcing them to apologise, after which those apologies are being accepted by the PM.“There is no question of the youngsters apologising… I am very proud of them and what thousands of them did… They defended the Constitution and protected the idea of India and India’s future,” Rahul said.The Congress leader held a “freewheeling” discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. It included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks” at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Farah Naaz alleged that in police detention, she faced communal barbs with a cop even calling her “anti-national”. Muskan said she was being assumed to be a Muslim which makes an Indian a “fair game”, even clarifying that she is a Hindu. Nutan Toppo said a pellet gun was fired at her.The leader of opposition’s decision to meet the youngsters to 10, Janpath, for a chat further upped the ante in the “BJP vs opposition” confrontation that has jammed the ongoing monsoon session of parliament.Continuing its aggression, a large contingent of opposition MPs marched inside the Parliament complex to protest the “absence of Amit Shah from parliament” and “Ayodhya donation scam”. The group included Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Dharmendra Yadav, Supriya Sule, NK Premachandran, Sagarika Ghose, Amar Singh, Chowdry Mohd Ramzan, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Naseer Hussain, K Radhakrishnan.Rahul held a placard with a face riddled with pellet gun injuries and a question “who gave the order?” The members also sought statehood for J&K.Addressing the media with the youngsters, Rahul said, “They are so young and standing before the media. But the prime minister and the home minister have no courage to stand before the press."He attacked home minister Amit Shah by saying that he is responsible for the crackdown on youngsters but “he does not have the decency to come to the Parliament, and the courage to comment on what happened.”Rahul took a jibe at PM Narendra Modi for saying that he has forgiven the students.
Article Summary: The Congress leader held a “freewheeling’ discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. The group included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks”

Article Title: BJP MLA alleges Mulund DP road incorporated into private project, seeks probe
Article Text:
Mumbai





: Mulund BJP MLA Mihir Kotecha has alleged that a Development Plan (DP) road linking LBS Marg between Off Park Road and Tansa Pipeline in Mulund West does not actually exist and was illegally incorporated into a developer’s project. Claiming that public property has been “stolen”, he has filed a complaint with Mulund police and demanded that the missing road, which would have helped reduce traffic congestion, be traced and handed over to BMC.Kotecha said the DP road is public property and is important for reducing traffic congestion. Under municipal corporation rules, he said, such roads are required to remain in BMC’s possession and be available for public use. He alleged that while a portion of the DP road has been constructed, the remaining stretch has disappeared and a nearly 60-storey building now stands on the site.In a representation submitted to senior police inspector of Mulund police station, Kotecha stated that the DP road between Off Park Road and Tansa pipeline on LBS Marg (plot numbers 543, 544 and 547, Nahur village) forms part of the approved Development Plan. He alleged that although part of the road has been developed, the remaining stretch is not physically available and has instead been incorporated into the developer’s project.
Article Summary: Mulund BJP MLA Mihir Kotecha has alleged that a Development Plan (DP) road linking LBS Marg and Tansa Pipeline in Mulund West does not actually exist. He has filed a complaint with Mulund police and demanded that the missing road, which would have helped reduce traffic congestion, be traced.

Article Title: Bombay high court grants bail to Solapur BJP corporator in MNS politician murder case
Article Text:
Police personnel took BJP Solapur corporator Shalan Shinde from jail to a polling booth to cast her vote for the recent MLC election

Kolhapur:





The Bombay high court’s Kolhapur bench has granted bail to Solapur Municipal Corporation’s BJP corporator Shalan Shankar Shinde, who is one of the accused in the murder of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena students’ wing city chief Balasaheb Sarwade earlier this year.Shinde was arrested along with seven others, including her husband, sons, sister and supporters, following Sarwade’s murder on Jan 2. According to the prosecution, Sarwade had filed his nomination for the Solapur Municipal Corporation elections and was allegedly pressured to withdraw it. Though he withdrew his candidature, he allegedly confronted the Shinde family over the treatment meted out to his relatives shortly before he was killed.Shinde subsequently won the civic election while in judicial custody and had recently been permitted to cast her vote in the MLC election. After her sister, Sharda Shinde, secured bail, Shalan Shinde approached the high court seeking regular bail. The plea was opposed by the prosecution and by Bajirao Pandurang Sarwade, brother of the deceased.“The applicant is a prominent resident of the area and is a sitting corporator.The applicant has deep roots in the society and is not a flight risk. The applicant also does not have criminal antecedents. The applicant is ready to abide by any condition that may be imposed by this court. The applicant may, therefore, be released on bail,” Shinde’s counsel argued before the court, according to the Aug 4 order.Opposing the plea, the prosecution and intervenor argued that Shinde was directly named in the FIR and had an active role in the crime.“The applicant is directly named in the FIR. The applicant is also attributed the role of throwing the chili powder. The applicant is also attributed exhortation to the other accused persons to kill deceased Balasaheb Sarwade... The offence is serious in nature. As the applicant is a sitting corporator, there is every likelihood that the applicant, if released on bail, may influence the witnesses,” they submitted.Granting bail, Justice Mehroz K Pathan noted discrepancies in eyewitness accounts and the limited role attributed to Shinde in the FIR.“The apprehensions of the learned APP as well as the learned counsel for the complainant can be taken care of by imposing stringent conditions upon the applicant. The applicant is a woman and has a family to look after. The investigation is complete and the chargesheet is filed. No fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the woman behind bars. Taking into consideration the limited role attributed to the applicant in the FIR and the material discrepancy, occurring in the statements of the eye witnesses, I am inclined to exercise discretion under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,” stated Justice Pathan before allowing the bail application and imposing conditions such as personal bond of Rs 1 lakh, showing up at police station once in two months and not entering the jurisdiction of the Jail Road police station untill framing of charges, except when required to mark her attendance.
Article Summary: Shalan Shankar Shinde is one of the accused in the murder of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena students’ wing city chief Balasaheb Sarwade earlier this year. She was arrested along with seven others, including her husband, sons, sister and supporters.

Article Title: Resident doctor among eight held in Solapur fake disability certificate racket
Article Text:
Police have arrested the doctor along with three alleged agents, two clerks and two beneficiaries

Kolhapur:





The Solapur city police have unearthed an alleged fake disability certificate racket operating from the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj District Civil Hospital and arrested eight people, including a resident medical officer, for allegedly issuing fraudulent documents used to secure or retain govt jobs.Among those arrested is Dr Satish Kanake, a 31-year-old resident medical officer, who was taken into custody on Monday night. A court has remanded him in police custody till Aug 7. The case was registered following a complaint lodged by dean Rutwik Devidas Jaykar on July 4.Police commissioner M Rajkumar said, “A man identified as Rajesh Bhausaheb Jadhav was issued a disability certificate to continue in his govt job. Following a complaint, an investigation found that he had obtained the certificate using a fake Aadhaar card. While the Aadhaar showed a Solapur address, he was actually a resident of Ahilyanagar.”Police have arrested the doctor along with three alleged agents, two clerks and two beneficiaries. The accused have been booked under sections 318(4), 337(3), 338, 340, 233, 235 and 2(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.According to the commissioner, scrutiny of certificates issued since Jan 2025 revealed suspicious irregularities. “Since Jan 2025, 3,714 divyang certificates were issued by the hospital. Of them, we have found that eight were suspiciously issued on fake documents and without verification by specialist doctors,” Rajkumar added.The arrested accused have been identified as Dr Satish Kanake, Rajesh Jadhav, Mahesh Bargaje, Rajesh Shavan, Vijay Garje, Arun Shimpi, Wasim Shaukat Khan and Sagar Rajput.The police said Rajput and Khan, both clerks at the hospital, were arrested on July 29. Dean Jaykar has initiated proceedings for their suspension, as govt rules mandate suspension of employees who remain in police custody for more than two days.The police said Bargaje, Garje and Shavan allegedly worked as agents from Ahilyanagar and have faced similar criminal cases in the past. The probe has also revealed manipulation of the certificate issuance process. To obtain a disability certificate, applicants must undergo both online and physical verification. An OTP required for online approval is sent to the dean’s mobile phone. The police alleged that Dr Kanake accessed the OTP and repeatedly used it to generate fake certificates.According to preliminary investigations, applicants were allegedly charged between Rs 3 lakh and Rs 5 lakh to obtain the certificates.
Article Summary: Dr Satish Kanake, a 31-year-old resident medical officer, was taken into custody on Monday night. The case was registered following a complaint lodged by dean Rutwik Devidas Jaykar on July 4. The police alleged that Dr Kanake accessed the OTP and repeatedly used it to generate fake certificates.

Article Title: Madras HC summons vigilance officer over failure to imprison convicted VAO
Article Text:
Madras HC summons vigilance officer over failure to imprison convicted VAO





Madurai: Madras high court has summoned the chief vigilance commissioner to explain the action taken against an investigation officer of the DVAC for failing to secure a former village administrative officer (VAO) in Madurai district, who was convicted in a case for accepting a bribe in 2008.The case of the prosecution is that P T M Pandiarajan was working as the VAO of Nadumuthalaikulam village in Madurai district. He was also in-charge of Panniyan, Kullaneri and Kannanur villages. In 2008, a person from Kannanur village approached Pandiarajan seeking an adangal copy of his land for obtaining a loan. Since Pandiarajan demanded a bribe, the person lodged a complaint with the DVAC officials. The DVAC arrested Pandiarajan when he received the bribe of Rs1,000 on July 11, 2008.In February 2018, the special court for trial of cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act in Madurai, convicted and sentenced Pandiarajan to two years imprisonment. Challenging the judgment, Pandiarajan preferred an appeal before HC. In May 2025, the HC modified the sentence to one year’s imprisonment and ordered Pandiarajan to be secured to undergo the sentence of imprisonment.The case was listed before the court under the caption ‘for reporting compliance’ on August 3. Justice K K Ramakrishnan observed that the court modified the sentence and ordered to sentence Pandiarajan in May 2025. Challenging the HC order, Pandiarajan preferred an appeal before the Supreme Court and the same was also dismissed in December 2025.The judge observed that despite the same, investigating officer Suriya Kala had not secured the accused to undergo the remaining period of imprisonment. Hence, the judge gave the direction to the chief vigilance commissioner to appear on August 10.
Article Summary: Madras HC summons vigilance officer over failure to imprison convicted VAO. P T M Pandiarajan was working as the VAO of Nadumuthalaikulam village in Madurai district. He was also in-charge of Panniyan, Kullaneri and Kannanur villages.

Article Title: HC orders desilting of Narasingam temple tank in six months
Article Text:
The Madras high court on Thursday directed the authorities to desilt the temple tank of the Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple at Narasingam in Madurai district within six months.

Madurai

:





The Madras high court on Thursday directed the authorities to desilt the temple tank of the Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple at Narasingam in Madurai district within six months.A division bench of Justice G R Swaminathan and Justice B Pugalendhi also directed the authorities to ensure that no garbage is dumped in or around the temple tank.The order was passed while disposing of a public interest litigation filed by J Kanagaraj of Madurai. The petitioner submitted that the ancient temple tank, located next to the historic rock-cut cave temple at Narasingam near Othakadai, had not been desilted for several years. As a result, it had become heavily silted and overgrown with bushes and weeds, while its retaining walls had deteriorated due to poor maintenance.He also alleged that garbage and plastic waste were being dumped in and around the tank, creating an unhygienic environment, affecting the sanctity of the temple premises and posing a health hazard to devotees.Recording the submissions, the bench directed the authorities to complete the desilting work within six months and ensure that no waste is dumped in or around the temple tank.
Article Summary: The Madras high court on Thursday directed the authorities to desilt the temple tank of the Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple at Narasingam in Madurai district within six months. The order was passed while disposing of a public interest litigation filed by J Kanagaraj of Madurai. The petitioner submitted that the ancient temple tank had not been desilted for several years.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Govt officials deliberately leaked prosecution sanction order in cashew corp graft case, says Kerala HC
Article Text:
The bench accordingly adjourned the petition to Sept 2

Kochi

:





The high court on Thursday orally remarked that govt officials had deliberately leaked the prosecution sanction order to the accused in a CBI case alleging large-scale corruption in the import and purchase of cashew nuts by Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation (KSCDC).The bench of Justice A Badharudeen was considering a petition filed by K M Shajahan of Thiruvananthapuram challenging the continuation of K A Ratheesh, the former managing director of the corporation and the second accused in the case, in three key posts under the state govt. The petitioner also sought a directive to conduct an inquiry into the alleged leakage of the prosecution sanction order. According to him, R Chandrasekharan, the former chairman of the corporation and the first accused, had displayed a copy of the order at a press conference even before it was presented before the court for approval. Expressing concern over the alleged leakage, the court observed that the state govt should exercise caution while appointing officials to key posts to prevent corruption.Shajahan contended that Ratheesh continued to hold the posts of secretary of the Kerala khadi and village industries board, managing director of RUTRONIX (Kerala state rural women’s electronics industrial co-operative federation Ltd) and chief executive officer of the Kerala khadi workers’ welfare fund board despite facing criminal prosecution in the corruption case.During the hearing, the state govt informed the court that Ratheesh had resigned from all three posts on Aug 3. It also submitted that action was being taken on the petitioner’s complaint regarding the alleged leakage of the prosecution sanction order dated July 2, which was subsequently modified on July 6. The bench accordingly adjourned the petition to Sept 2.
Article Summary: The high court orally remarked that govt officials had deliberately leaked the prosecution sanction order to the accused in a CBI case. The bench of Justice A Badharudeen was considering a petition filed by K M Shajahan of Thiruvananthapuram challenging the continuation of K A Ratheesh in three key posts under the state govt.

Article Title: Three held for raping minor in Pathanamthitta
Article Text:
Kottayam

:





Police have arrested three persons for allegedly sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl over an extended period, following information from the Pathanamthitta district child helpline.Malayalapuzha police registered cases under Pocso Act after the child helpline alerted them regarding the case.Those arrested, all natives of Malayalappuzha, allegedly assaulted the child repeatedly since 2023-24.Acting on the complaint, police under SHO inspector Shafi B M formed multiple teams and arrested the three. The accused were produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Malayalapuzha police registered cases under Pocso Act after the child helpline alerted them regarding the case. Those arrested, all natives of Malayalappuzha, allegedly assaulted the child repeatedly since 2023-24. The accused were produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Govt cancels R Sugathan’s escort parole plea
Article Text:
BJP councillor R Sugathan

Thiruvananthapuram

:





The state govt has cancelled the plea for an escort parole submitted by BJP Thiruvananthapuram Corporation councillor R Sugathan, who is currently lodged in Viyyur jail.The home department issued an order stating that govt had reviewed the matter following a communication from the local self-govt department (LSGD). The department had earlier informed govt that it has cancelled the earlier recommendation given in favour of Sugathan.Sugathan had submitted an application seeking parole and govt had earlier rejected his parole application through an order dated July 13.Subsequently, based on the recommendation contained in the department’s July 18 note, govt issued a response to Sugathan on July 20 favouring him.However, after LSGD informed govt that its earlier note had been cancelled, the home department reconsidered the matter.Govt has now cancelled the response issued to Sugathan. However, the earlier decision rejecting his parole application remains in force, the order clarified.
Article Summary: State govt has cancelled the plea for an escort parole submitted by BJP Thiruvananthapuram Corporation councillor R Sugathan. Sugathan is currently lodged in Viyyur jail. The home department issued an order stating that govt had reviewed the matter following a communication from the local self-govt department.
